explanation: One of the twelve tribes of Israel, chosen by God to perform special religious duties and serve in the temple.
King David was the second king of Israel and a central figure in the Old Testament. He is known for his victory over Goliath and his strong relationship with God.
Work or tasks carried out for God and His people, especially within the framework of religious life in Israel.
One of the four main groups of Levites, descended from Kohath, one of Levi's sons. They had specific responsibilities in the temple.
The eldest son of Levi and ancestor of one of the four main groups of Levites. His descendants also had specific responsibilities in the temple.
Another son of Levi and ancestor of one of the four main groups of Levites. The Merarites also had specific responsibilities in the temple.
A leader among the Levites and head of the Kohathites during David's time. He was responsible for transporting and caring for holy objects in the temple.
